The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Severe yellowing and large brown necrotic areas
- Necrosis starting from the leaf margin, spreading inward in a V-shaped pattern
- Yellow tissue remaining at the top/base of the leaf
- Severely wilted, collapsed leaf tissue

This pattern strongly suggests **Verticillium Wilt** — V-shaped lesions starting at the leaf margin with brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing is the hallmark symptom.

Let me view one reference image to confirm:

The reference image is a near-perfect match to the test image:
- Same V-shaped brown necrotic lesion starting at the leaf margin
- Same yellow tissue surrounding the brown necrotic area
- Same overall leaf morphology and disease pattern
- Same white background (similar image source)

The test image simply shows a more advanced/desiccated stage of the same disease.

{"prediction": "Verticillium_Wilt", "confidence": 0.88, "reasoning": "The test image shows a tomato leaf with a large V-shaped brown necrotic lesion starting at the leaf margin, surrounded by yellow tissue — the hallmark of Verticillium Wilt. The reference image (LeafNet_265.jpg) matches almost exactly in lesion shape, color pattern (brown necrosis + yellow halo), and leaf morphology. No concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), no powdery coating (ruling out Powdery Mildew), no discrete small spots (ruling out Septoria/Bacterial Speck)."}
